text:
Maria: Quick flag — on a long-context generation replay (90k token session) I saw KV resident climb from 38GB -> 72GB and OOM near the end, but free list shows lots of tiny holes. Likely fragmentation not pure leak.
Jan: Yikes. Any profiler snapshots?
Maria: Pushed a heap snapshot and kv-snapshot logs to /tmp/kv-dumps/node6-1719504321.tar.gz (s3 link: https://s3.company/kv-dumps/node6-1719504321). Key bits below:
```
KV pool: 96GB
Allocated: 72.1GB
Active chunks: 49.5GB
Free fragments: 22.6GB (avg size 384 bytes)
Large contiguous free: 1.2GB
Metadata overhead: 1.8GB
Fragmentation ratio (frag/allocated): 31%
Small-chunk count: 58M
```
Lee: Hmm avg fragment 384b — allocator is currently 512b base-step buddy. That suggests a lot of split paths creating micro-fragments. Which allocator version?
Maria: Buddy-v2 (rolled last week). Alan ran the rollout on canary.
Alan: Confirmed — canary hosts show similar pattern on long contexts. Short requests look fine.
Jan: Two hypotheses: 1) block-size quantization map too coarse causing many splits; 2) eviction/aging prefers newest-first and leaves many small stale holes.
Lee: I ran a quick sim: feeding longcontexts with repeated small KV updates produces chain of splits. GC/compaction only triggers when free crosses 20GB threshold, which we hit late.
Maria: Repro script: `./tools/kv_replay --trace long_context_session.log --rate 1 --kv-updates 200k` — reproduces in ~40 mins on canary.
Alan: Suggestion: experiment with smaller base block (256b) vs larger (1kb) and measure fragmentation and perf. Also try eager micro-compact that coalesces adjacent free fragments under low load.
Jan: Also consider changing eviction policy from LRU-newest to time-windowed LRU to prefer coalescing evict targets. Right now we're evicting whatever has lowest score, leaving many interleaved small frees.
Lee: Agreed. Proposed experiment matrix:
- A: base 512b (current) + threshold 20GB (control)
- B: base 256b + micro-compact disabled
- C: base 1024b + background coalesce (interval 30s)
- D: base 512b + eager micro-compact when free fragments > 8M
Each run: replay the same trace, capture resident, frag %, tail-latency, throughput.
Maria: TL;DR expectations: smaller base reduces waste from splits but increases metadata overhead; larger base reduces fragment count but may increase internal waste for many tiny KV entries. Need numbers.
Alan: I'll spin up 4 canaries (A-D) in us-west2 and tag them kv-frag-exp-171950. Can we add extra tracing to capture contiguous free runs?
Lee: I'll add a metric: `kv.free_runs.count_by_length` and `kv.fragmentation.hist` (exponential buckets). Also emit `kv.compact.ops` with duration.
Jan: One more angle — kernel selection and batching heuristics could be exacerbating this: continuous-batch loop holds many KV pointers longer (in-flight sequences) which pins allocations and prevents coalescing. We should correlate high in-flight token windows with fragmentation spikes.
Maria: Good call. I saw spikes aligning with batch-window 512 -> try lowering batching window on one experiment to 256 and measure.
Alan: Running jobs now. ETA ~2.5 hours to get initial numbers. I'll post logs. deploy-bot: can you annotate canary group once ready?
deploy-bot: Canary group kv-frag-exp-171950 created, 4 instances booting (us-west2), expected ready in ~8m.
Maria: For rollout guidance: if C shows >30% reduction in fragmentation w/ <5% perf regression, that's a win. If D (eager compact) reduces fragmentation but adds >10% p95, we should consider throttled compaction during low load only.
Lee: Also add a test for long GC pauses: ensure compaction doesn't block hot path. Use non-blocking incremental relink.
Jan: I'll draft a short RFC with experiment results and recommendation: change quantization map + background micro-coalesce + eviction tweak. Aim for canary -> staged rollout over 2 weeks.
Maria: Thanks — will watch the canaries. If anyone notices production regressions, ping #eng-oncall. :eyes:
Alan: I'll post the first perf plots when done.
Maria: great, thanks everyone.
